prompt.context: Your client, SneakyChat, is a wildly popular Silicon Valley startup with a rapidly growing user base. SneakyChat's App allows users to send expiring pictures as well as connect with local people in their area. A potential acquirer has offered to purchase the Company for $500m, but on the condition that the Company will generate $2m in cumulative net income over the next 3 months, and have at least 700k daily active users as of the end of month 3. SneakyChat's CFO has hired you to help hit these metrics.
prompt.question: How would you help SneakyChat achieve $2m in cumulative net income and at least 700k daily active users by the end of month 3 in order to satisfy the acquisition conditions?

clarifying_info.a: SneakyChat currently only operates in the US.

clarifying_info.q: Does SneakyChat currently generate any revenue?
clarifying_info.a: No current revenue — the company has focused solely on user growth and not monetization.

clarifying_info.q: When did the company start operations?
clarifying_info.a: The company started operations this year.

clarifying_info.q: Are the net income and daily active user targets cumulative or end-of-period?
clarifying_info.a: Net income is cumulative over the 3 months; daily active users is the total as of the end of month 3.

clarifying_info.q: Should we factor in user attrition?
clarifying_info.a: Normally it would be considered, but for simplicity assume no user attrition.

exhibits.title: Current Operations
exhibits.shows: A table of SneakyChat's current monthly operating metrics including daily active users, revenue, and cost line items.

exhibits.title: Marketing Proposal — SirSalesAlot Marketing Co.
exhibits.shows: A table of five marketing options with new users added per month (months 1-3) and cost per month (months 1-3), plus a footnote that current cash on hand is $3m at the beginning of month 1 and that the Super Bowl Ad requires full marketing team resources precluding any other strategy.

framework: Understand the two acquisition hurdles: $2m cumulative net income and 700k daily active users by end of month 3
Assess current baseline: 100k users, $0 revenue, $200k/mo costs (all fixed except marketing)
Identify gap: need +600k users and need to move from -$200k/mo to cumulative +$2m net income
Determine revenue strategy: brainstorm monetization options, then apply selected revenue model to calculate revenue
Determine user acquisition strategy: brainstorm growth options, evaluate marketing proposals against cash constraint and ROI
Model combined financials (revenue from growing user base minus fixed costs minus marketing spend) month by month
Select optimal marketing mix and confirm both hurdles are met
State recommendation with risks and next steps

questions.prompt: Given current operations (Exhibit 1), what is SneakyChat's baseline financial situation and what must change to meet the acquisition conditions?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify: 100k current daily active users vs. 700k target (gap of 600k); $0 revenue vs. need to generate cumulative $2m net income; fixed costs of $200k/mo (employees $150k + rent $50k) with no marketing spend currently. Net income is -$200k/mo. Without revenue, costs alone produce -$600k over 3 months, so both monetization AND user growth are needed.

math.setup: Current monthly net income = Revenue - Total Costs = $0 - $200k = -$200k. Over 3 months with no change: cumulative NI = -$600k.
math.answer: -$600k cumulative net income with no change; $2.6m improvement needed

questions.prompt: Brainstorm ways SneakyChat could generate revenue from its user base.
questions.guidance: Strong candidates will think across multiple monetization buckets: advertising (in-app ads, sponsored content, banner ads), data monetization (selling anonymized user data, behavioral insights to third parties), premium/subscription features (premium filters, expanded storage, ad-free tier), partnerships and integrations (brand partnerships, local business promotions), e-commerce/transactions (in-app purchases, virtual goods). After the brainstorm, interviewer reveals: the company has selected two approaches — (1) selling ads generates $1.50/user/month and (2) selling data generates $0.50/user/month, both net of associated costs, totaling $2.00/user/month.

questions.prompt: Using the selected monetization model ($2/user/month), calculate monthly and cumulative revenue and net income before any new marketing spend, then determine what minimum user growth is needed.
questions.guidance: With existing 100k users monetized at $2/user/mo, monthly revenue = $200k, which exactly offsets fixed costs of $200k. So current users break even but generate $0 net income. All net income must come from incremental users. Candidate should recognize that revenue compounds as users are cumulative (no attrition assumed).

math.setup: Monthly revenue = cumulative users x $2/user/month. Fixed costs = $200k/month. Monthly NI = Revenue - $200k - monthly marketing cost.
steps: Month 1 baseline (100k users, no new marketing): Revenue = 100k x $2 = $200k; Costs = $200k; NI = $0
Net income from new users = (new cumulative users) x $2 - marketing costs
math.answer: Existing 100k users break even. All $2m+ cumulative net income must come from new users acquired via marketing.

questions.prompt: Brainstorm ways SneakyChat could acquire new users.
questions.guidance: Strong candidates will consider: organic/viral growth (referral programs, social sharing incentives), paid digital marketing (search ads, social media ads, influencer partnerships), offline/event marketing (pop-up events, campus activations, onsite activations), partnerships (integration with other apps, telecom bundles), geographic expansion (international markets), acquiring a competitor or complementary app. After brainstorm, interviewer provides Exhibit 2.

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 2, evaluate the marketing options and determine which combination(s) can meet the user and net income targets. Note the $3m cash-on-hand constraint at the start of Month 1.
questions.guidance: Candidate should first screen out infeasible options: (1) Acquire Competitor costs $3,500k in Month 1 alone, exceeding the $3m cash on hand — eliminate. (2) Print Ads add only 50k users/month at $75k/month cost ($225k total for 150k cumulative users); at $2/user revenue that generates $300k + $600k + $900k = $600k net revenue but costs $225k, yielding $375k net contribution — but combined with other options it adds cost per user that exceeds incremental revenue, making it less efficient (net contribution per user is lower than other options). Candidate should calculate net income for viable combinations. Key insight: users are cumulative, so revenue in month 2 includes month 1 users, and month 3 includes months 1+2 users. Preferred answer: Online Ads + Onsite Activations. Super Bowl is viable but riskier (footnote: optimistic estimates, full team required).

math.setup: For each marketing option, calculate cumulative users by month, monthly revenue (cumulative users x $2), monthly costs ($200k fixed + marketing), and monthly/cumulative net income. Starting users = 100k.
steps: Online Ads alone: Month 1 users=225k, Rev=$450k, Costs=$300k, NI=$150k | Month 2 users=350k, Rev=$700k, Costs=$300k, NI=$400k | Month 3 users=475k, Rev=$950k, Costs=$300k, NI=$650k | Cumulative NI=$1,200k — insufficient (only 475k users, not 700k)

Onsite Activations alone: Month 1=200k, Rev=$400k, Costs=$300k, NI=$100k | Month 2=300k, Rev=$600k, Costs=$300k, NI=$300k | Month 3=400k, Rev=$800k, Costs=$300k, NI=$500k | Cumulative NI=$900k — insufficient

Online Ads + Onsite Activations: Month 1 users=325k, Rev=$650k, Costs=$400k, NI=$250k | Month 2=550k, Rev=$1,100k, Costs=$400k, NI=$700k | Month 3=775k, Rev=$1,550k, Costs=$400k, NI=$1,150k | Cumulative NI=$2,100k | End users=775k > 700k — BOTH HURDLES MET
Print Ads alone: Month 1=150k, Rev=$300k, Costs=$275k, NI=$25k | Month 2=200k, Rev=$400k, Costs=$275k, NI=$125k | Month 3=250k, Rev=$500k, Costs=$275k, NI=$225k | Cumulative NI=$375k — insufficient
Online + Print + Onsite: Cumulative NI meets hurdle and users exceed 700k, but print is least efficient — good candidate notes resources could be redeployed
Acquire Competitor: Month 1 cost=$3,500k exceeds $3m cash — eliminate immediately

Super Bowl Ad (standalone, Month 3 only): Month 1=100k users (no new), Rev=$200k, Costs=$200k, NI=$0 | Month 2=100k users, Rev=$200k, Costs=$200k, NI=$0 | Month 3=1,600k users, Rev=$3,200k, Costs=$1,200k, NI=$2,000k | Cumulative NI=$2,000k — barely meets $2m hurdle; users=1,600k > 700k; but riskier (optimistic estimates, footnote caveat)
math.answer: Online Ads + Onsite Activations: cumulative NI = $2,100k (exceeds $2m), end-of-month-3 users = 775k (exceeds 700k). This is the preferred combination.

brainstorming.prompt: First brainstorm: How could SneakyChat generate revenue from its existing and future user base? Second brainstorm: How could SneakyChat acquire new users?

categories.name: Monetization — Advertising
ideas: Targeted local business ads (leveraging the 'connect with local people' feature)
Video ads before or between content

categories.name: Monetization — Data
ideas: Selling anonymized user behavioral data to third parties
Providing market research insights to brands

categories.name: Monetization — Premium Features
ideas: Expanded location radius for connecting with people

categories.name: User Acquisition — Events and Offline
ideas: Onsite activations at college campuses, concerts, sporting events
Street teams in high-density urban areas

categories.name: User Acquisition — Viral and Organic
ideas: Referral programs (invite a friend, unlock a feature)

categories.name: User Acquisition — Partnerships and M&A
ideas: Integration or partnership with complementary apps
Acquiring a competitor or complementary user base

recommendation: Recommend that SneakyChat immediately monetize all users at $2/user/month (ads + data selling) and pursue the Online Ads + Onsite Activations marketing strategy to grow the user base
This combination will deliver cumulative net income of approximately $2.1m and 775k daily active users by end of month 3, exceeding both acquisition hurdles
risks: Marketing firm projections (SirSalesAlot) tend to be optimistic — actual user growth may fall short of estimates
Revenue per user assumptions ($2/user/month) may not hold if user engagement declines or monetization implementation takes time
Starting monetization simultaneously with growth campaigns could reduce user experience and increase churn (attrition assumed zero but is a real risk)
Acquisition deal terms could change or acquirer could walk away even if targets are met
Concentrated reliance on a single marketing vendor creates execution risk
next_steps: Immediately implement the ads and data monetization infrastructure to begin generating revenue from the existing 100k user base
Finalize contract with SirSalesAlot for Online Ads and Onsite Activations, beginning Month 1
Establish weekly tracking dashboards for daily active users and cumulative net income against the acquisition hurdles
Build contingency plan if user growth falls below projections (e.g., layer in Print Ads or optimize conversion from existing campaigns)
Begin due diligence preparation for the acquisition to ensure smooth close once metrics are achieved
